summary: Paro International Airport is the sole international gateway to the Kingdom of Bhutan, nestled in a deep valley at roughly 7,300 feet elevation and surrounded by Himalayan peaks reaching 18,000 feet. Widely regarded as one of the most challenging airports in the world to land at, only a handful of specially certified pilots are authorized to operate there, navigating tight turns between mountains before the final descent. The approach and departure paths demand precise execution, making every flight at Paro a memorable experience.
faqs:
Q: Why is Paro Airport considered one of the world's most dangerous airports?
A: It is surrounded by peaks up to 18,000 feet and lies in a narrow valley with no room for go-arounds. Pilots must execute sharp manual turns and visual approaches in variable weather, so only certified captains may land there.

Q: Which airlines operate at Paro International Airport?
A: Druk Air (the national carrier) and Bhutan Airlines are the main operators, with flights connecting to cities like Bangkok, Delhi, Kolkata, Kathmandu, and Singapore.

Q: What is the elevation of Paro Airport?
A: The airport sits at approximately 7,300 feet (2,225 meters) above sea level, which affects aircraft performance and requires careful load calculations.

Q: Can private jets or non-scheduled flights land at Paro?
A: Only pilots personally approved by the airlines operating at Paro are permitted to land there. Non-scheduled operations require special coordination and qualified crew.
transport_tips: The airport is about 6 km from Paro town, and taxis are readily available outside the terminal; the ride takes roughly 15 minutes. Pre-arranged hotel transfers or guided transport are strongly recommended, as Bhutan requires tourists to have a licensed guide and pre-booked itinerary. Thimphu, the capital, is approximately 50 km away and around 1.5 hours by road.
local_tip: Sit on the left side of the aircraft when flying into Paro for the best views of the Himalayan ridgelines and the dramatic final turn over the valley walls, and on the right side for takeoff.
